brief.headline: Close the ₹28644 overpay on PET bottles and shift 30-day terms to 15 days to free up ₹46539 cash — they're steady but we're tiny (0.02%) so name two big alternates to show we can walk.

priceAsk.summary: Cut the PET 100ml amber bottle from ₹2.18 to ₹1.87 per piece, matching Suraj Blow Plast.
priceAsk.basis: We pay Suraj ₹1.87 for the same bottle; TPAC charges ₹2.18 — a 16.6% gap. Market data shows PP caps have modest room to drop at higher volume, so bottles should too.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is healthy — ₹637.48 Cr revenue, they keep about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell (3.8%), rated [ICRA] A / Stable, and they borrow money at about 10.27%. Their cash is stuck for 79 days (same as peers at 79d), but they pay suppliers in just 17 days versus the peer norm of 33 — so they could ease up and still be faster than most. The catch: we're 0.02% of their sales (₹11.32 L), so on our own we have almost no pull. Bundle this negotiation with a longer commitment or bring in a second source to show we're serious about switching if they won't move.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹0.31 per bottle (16.6%) versus our best price.
Shifting payment from 30 to 15 days frees up cash for us.
They borrow at about 10%; paying them 15 days early costs us roughly 5% annualized — they save that much, so trade it for a price cut.
We are a tiny customer — 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue.
Market data: PP caps at ₹0.85–0.95 typical, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — bottles should follow the same logic.
They pay suppliers in 17 days, much faster than the peer norm of 33 — room to stretch terms without hurting them.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate, health score B (65/100).

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr) — pails, containers, pharma. Strong and profitable (B 73/100), a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd (Pearlpet)
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (₹19.83 Cr) — direct fit for PET bottles, though smaller and weaker health (D 24/100); worth a quote to pressure price.

risks: We're 0.02% of their sales — too small to matter alone. If we don't bundle volume, commit long-term, or show a credible switch plan (RFQ to Manjushree or Mold-Tek), they'll ignore us.
They have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays flagged — not deal-breakers with an A rating, but watch for any sign these get worse (could mean cash or compliance trouble brewing).
Their Altman Z-score is 2.77 (grey zone) — not distressed, but not rock-solid either. Don't push so hard on price that we destabilize a sole source; line up Manjushree first.
Faster payment (15 days) helps them save 10.27% borrowing cost — but only if we tie it explicitly to a price cut. If we give terms for free, we lose leverage and cash with no gain.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the gap on the PET bottle — Suraj gives us ₹1.87 and you're at ₹2.18 — and in return we'll move to 15-day payment, which saves you about 10% in borrowing cost; let's find the middle that works for both of us.
